etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English kepere, equivalent to keep +‎ -er.

definitions.definition: One who remains or keeps in a place or position.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Titus 2:5:
1971, H. R. F. Keating, The Strong Man:
quote.text: I was not altogether surprised: they seemed to be, even more than people in the surrounding wolds, stolid keepers-to-themselves, impossible to stir, dourly determined to stick to the firm routine of their lives […]

definitions.definition: A fruit or vegetable that keeps (remains good) for some time without spoiling.

quote.citation: c. 1847, Andrew Jackson Downing, The Fruits and Fruit Trees of America:
1878, Journal of Horticulture and Practical Gardening, volume 35, page 331:
quote.text: And mark you, good keepers are some years bad keepers, as this year; and a hard, heavy, unbruisable Apple that really will keep to late on in the season is doubly valuable.

definitions.definition: (informal) A person or thing worth keeping.

quote.text: "Okay, that's a keeper," Harold said as he netted the 3-pounder and put him on a stringer over the side of the boat.

quote.citation: 2005, Ladies' Home Journal, volume 122, numbers 7-12, page 101:
quote.text: When he brought me home and volunteered to come with me while I walked my dog, Max, I knew he was a keeper.

quote.citation: 2008, Jennifer Zomar, A Candle for the Children, page 28:
quote.text: We hadn't dated for long when he said those three magic words: "I'll cook tonight." I knew he was a keeper.

quote.citation: 2023 September 30, HarryBlank, “Meeting in the Middle”, in SCP Foundation‎[1], archived from the original on 25 May 2024:
quote.text: He sucked in a deep breath, then opened his eyes and searched for hers. "So what do you figure? Alternate universe?"She nodded. "Yeah. Real bad one. Not at all a keeper."

definitions.definition: A person charged with guarding or caring for, storing, or maintaining something; a custodian, a guard; sometimes a gamekeeper.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Genesis 4:9:
quote.text: And the Lord said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother's keeper?

quote.citation: 1907 January, Harold Bindloss, chapter 4, in The Dust of Conflict, 1st Canadian edition, Toronto, Ont.: McLeod & Allen, →OCLC:
quote.text: The inquest on keeper Davidson was duly held, and at the commencement seemed likely to cause Tony Palliser less anxiety than he had expected.

definitions.definition: (sports) The player charged with guarding a goal or wicket. Short form of goalkeeper, wicketkeeper. In quidditch (both Muggle quidditch and the game in the original Harry Potter series), this is someone responsible for guarding the three goalposts.[1]

quote.citation: 2011 June 4, Phil McNulty, “England 2 - 2 Switzerland”, in BBC‎[2]:
quote.text: England should have capitalised on their growing momentum to win, but Darren Bent failed to reproduce the finishing touches that have brought him goals in three successive appearances. He was blocked by Diego Benaglio when he was played in by Wilshere then blazed over the top of an open goal late on after Young's shot was saved by Switzerland's keeper.

definitions.definition: At Eton College, a student who is the captain of a sport or an activity such as drama.
A part of a mechanism that catches or retains another part, for example the part of a door lock that fits in the frame and receives the bolt.
A thin, flexible tress or tongue of material (e.g. leather) at the end of a crop opposite the handle, which is broad enough to prevent the horse's skin from being marked as it might be by a whip.

quote.citation: 1912, Minnie McIntyre, Edward E. Wood, Alexander Henry Waddell, Wilfred Jay, Wilfred P. Pond, Bit & Spur, page 39:
quote.text: The all-whalebone crop, braided with gut, pigskin handle, single brown stitched leather keeper, and close […]

quote.citation: 2022 February 22, Gretchen Felker-Martin, Manhunt, Tor Nightfire, →ISBN:
quote.text: “When we catch you—”   A brief but vivid fantasy of the nose-ringed girl trailing a riding crop's cool leather keeper over her clenched and trembling ass shoved its way eagerly into Fran's imagination.   “—we're gonna […] ”

definitions.definition: (American football) An offensive play in which the quarterback runs toward the goal with the ball after it is snapped.
Synonym of armature (“piece of metal connecting the poles of a magnet to preserve its strength by forming a circuit”)

quote.citation: 1878, Oluf Andreas Løwold Pihl, On Magnets (page 94)
quote.text: The continuous lines indicate the moments, when the magnet and keeper of equal diameter (10.5mm) act upon each other  […]
